Recover subscriptions that lose their transport
entries.note:
Adjacent to #4405: both edit packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/client.ts and its
test, and this is the only other topic that touches subscription lifecycle.

A durable subscription that dies with a transport error drains and waits for a
session the supervisor never produces unless the socket reports closed, so the
environment silently stops updating until the client restarts. Root cause behind
#4589; #4593 only recovers the settle path.

entries.label: t3code/client-suite
entries.summary: Complete client-only desktop, pairing, environment presentation, and settings suite
entries.note:
Canonical cumulative client branch. Subsumes #4444, #4474, #4496, #4505,
#4538, #4548, #4559, #4567, the branch-linked
t3code/show-remote-host-name topic, and the diagnostics work from #4486.

a local owner or remote client.

entries.label: t3code/unify-environment-selection
entries.summary: Align settings ownership and environment selection across settings pages
entries.note:
Places the shared environment selector inside the Environment navigation group
and repeats it in a clearly labeled scope strip on environment-owned pages.
Keybindings are client-owned and client-persisted; Connections remains a
client page. Assistant output and new-thread/worktree defaults are client-owned
across web, desktop, and mobile. Provider configuration, host paths, source
control, and diagnostics remain environment-owned.

entries.summary: Fix quadratic thread-reopen replay: batch client apply + cap server resume gap
entries.note:
Fixes #4596. Reopening a thread with a large event backlog re-replayed the whole
backlog: the server streamed every event past the client's cursor individually,
and the client re-derived the full timeline per event.

Placed before #4599 because it restructures ChatView.tsx -- extracting the
timeline derivation into threadTimelineModel.ts -- and #4599's find bar is
additive UI on top of that file. Restructure first, then build on the final
shape.

Touches ws.ts and client-runtime state/threads.ts, which #4405, #4593 and #4602
also edit, so it merges after all three have landed.

entries.label: t3code/mobile-thread-replay-render-fixes
entries.summary: Cut mobile thread-reopen replay churn in the feed pipeline
entries.note:
The mobile-only layers left over after #4605: incremental, identity-cached
thread-feed derivation in threadActivity.ts, no layout animations or animated
end-scrolls or streaming haptics during a backlog catch-up, and code
highlighting withheld while a message is still streaming.

Last in the manifest and mobile-only -- apps/mobile plus its t3-markdown-text
module -- so it has no overlap with the web/client-runtime topics above it.
Depends on #4605 conceptually, not textually: #4605 fixes the shared
subscription path, this one fixes what mobile still re-derives on top of it.

Branch-linked, not PR-linked: #4624 was closed upstream without merging, so
the BRANCH is authoritative and this entry must not be dropped just because the
PR is closed. Carried because the replay cost is real on this phone. Its head carries a follow-up commit past the PR: the PR's 200ms
highlight debounces could never fire, because a growing code block's React key
encodes its source offsets and the block remounts on every delta.

entries.summary: Render markdown images from workspace files
entries.note:
ChatMarkdown had no img renderer, so a markdown image with a local path
rendered broken: the web origin only serves the client bundle, so the request
hit the SPA fallback and decoded as HTML. Local sources now resolve through the
signed workspace-asset URL the file preview panel already uses.

Overlaps t3code/local/artifact-safety and #3984, which own the other half of
ChatMarkdown's image story -- but on the `code` renderer (inline code naming a
generated thread artifact), not `img`. The two are complementary, not competing:
this one handles markdown image syntax pointing at workspace files, that one
handles artifact references. Both import from ../assets/assetUrls, so expect a
small import-region conflict and nothing semantic.

Appended rather than placed next to those entries because they sit at the head
of the manifest and this arrived via extend. If ChatMarkdown accumulates a third
image-adjacent topic, cluster the three into a group instead.

entries.label: t3code-dedupe-environment-icon.patch
entries.summary: De-duplicate the EnvironmentIcon helper in BranchToolbarEnvironmentSelector
entries.note:
t3code/client-suite and t3code/unify-environment-selection each add the same
EnvironmentIcon helper to BranchToolbarEnvironmentSelector.tsx, one copy each.
Git merges both additions without conflict, so the assembled file ends up with
two byte-identical declarations and the web build fails with
"The symbol "EnvironmentIcon" has already been declared".

Stack-emergent by construction: neither branch is wrong on its own, and the
duplicate only exists once both are merged, so it cannot live on either topic.
Caught by the esbuild syntax gate, which is the only cheap check that sees it --
the content audit looks for MISSING lines, not duplicated ones.
